extracted.intended_audience: registrants, corporate accountants, auditors, and securities counsel preparing SEC filings involving business combinations
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on SEC reporting, filing, and financial‑statement requirements (S‑X, Form 8‑K, registration/proxy statements, Form 1‑A) applicable to business combinations, step acquisitions, drop‑downs and combinations under common control. Covers tests of significance (investment, income, asset), pro forma and when separate historical financial statements are required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulation A (Form 1‑A) scaled financial statement requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Part F/S of Form 1‑A directs issuers relying on Regulation A to present financial information of acquired or probable‑to‑be‑acquired businesses under S‑X Rule 8‑04 applicable to SRCs. Form 1‑A provides scaled requirements for the form and content of financial statements of an acquired or probable‑to‑be‑acquired business by Regulation A issuers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of scaling: financial statements may be unaudited, cover shorter periods, and do not need to be updated if the most recent balance sheet is not older than nine months.

rubrics_metrics.name: Step acquisitions — evaluate Rule 3‑05/Form 8‑K filing requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: An increase in the investment of an existing subsidiary (step acquisition) is considered the acquisition of a business; registrants need to evaluate whether such step acquisitions require filing of Rule 3‑05 financial statements on Form 8‑K and/or in a registration statement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interpretive response: It depends. An increase in an investment in a consolidated subsidiary does not ordinarily require filing separate financial statements because the consolidated financial statements already include the acquired business. However, pro forma financial information reflecting the impact of the transaction may be required.

rubrics_metrics.name: When separate historical financial statements are no longer required (S‑X Rule 3‑05(b)(4)(iii))
rubrics_metrics.description: Separate financial statements of the acquired business need not be presented once the operating results of the acquired business have been reflected in the audited post‑acquisition results of the registrant for a specified period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specified periods: nine months for an acquisition that exceeds 20% but does not exceed 40% significance; a complete fiscal year for an acquisition that exceeds 40% significance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scenarios that still require historical financial statements in step acquisitions
rubrics_metrics.description: Even for step acquisitions of previously consolidated subsidiaries, separate historical financial statements of the acquired business may be required in certain scenarios.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: (1) when the registrant’s consolidated financial statements filed with the SEC have not included the subsidiary for a sufficient period and separate financial statements of the acquired business have not been previously filed; (2) when S‑X Rule 3‑05 does not apply (e.g., preparing a merger proxy statement or Form S‑4 where the target's financial statements for the same periods required in an annual report apply).

rubrics_metrics.name: Pro forma financial information requirement (S‑X Rule 11‑01)
rubrics_metrics.description: Pro forma financial information reflecting the acquisition is required under S‑X Rule 11‑01(a)(8) when that pro forma information would be material to investors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even if the financial statements of the acquired business are not presented, pro forma financial information may be required if material. Example: registrant must file pro forma information on Form 8‑K for step acquisitions when it determines the information would be material to investors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indirect acquisitions (acquisitions by an acquired business) — materiality exception
rubrics_metrics.description: Acquisitions made by a business that the registrant acquired (indirect acquisitions) generally are not evaluated as if directly acquired by the registrant; S‑X Rule 3‑05 applies only to acquisitions made by the registrant or its predecessor(s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: However, registrants should provide financial information for indirect acquisitions when omission of that information would render the financial information of the directly acquired business misleading or substantially incomplete. Factors include size of the indirect acquisition relative to registrant, timing relative to registrant year‑end, and the length of the financial‑statement period that includes the indirect acquisition.

rubrics_metrics.name: When to include financial statements of significant equity‑method investees (S‑X Rule 3‑09 analogy)
rubrics_metrics.description: S‑X Rule 3‑09 requires separate financial statements for significant subsidiaries not consolidated and for 50% or less owned equity‑method investees when significance tests exceed 20%. S‑X Rule 3‑05 does not directly address whether separate financial statements of an acquired business’s equity‑method investees must be filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The SEC staff has required registrants to provide these financial statements if they are material to an investor’s understanding of the acquired business. Considerations include the significance of the equity‑method investee to the registrant, whether the investment was acquired during the most recent fiscal year, and whether the investment is the primary asset of the acquired business. SAB Topic 6K guidance for significance is relevant by analogy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accounting for combinations of entities under common control (as‑if pooling‑of‑interests)
rubrics_metrics.description: A combination of entities under common control is accounted for by recognizing net assets received at carrying amount and retrospectively revising all comparative periods presented (the as‑if pooling‑of‑interests method) when there is a change in reporting entity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If transferred equity interests or net assets meet the definition of a business, the transaction will generally result in the acquisition of a business for SEC reporting and the registrant must consider Form 8‑K and S‑X Rule 3‑05 filing requirements. After the combined 'new' reporting entity's restated financial statements are filed, separate financial statements of the acquired business are no longer required in a registration statement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Combination after balance sheet date — supplemental restated financial statements
rubrics_metrics.description: When a transaction accounted for as an as‑if pooling‑of‑interests is completed after the latest balance sheet date and before post‑combination operating results have been published, the registrant normally does not reflect the transaction in its pre‑acquisition financial statements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: However, the registrant may elect to provide or may be required to provide supplemental audited financial statements giving effect to the transaction (i.e., applied retrospectively in all comparative periods presented) in connection with registration or proxy statements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recasting prior filings for drop‑down transactions — timing and 'fundamental change' considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirements for recasting previously filed financial statements after drop‑down transactions (common control reorganizations) depend on the filing context and whether the transaction is a 'fundamental change.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Summary: initial registration statement (S‑1, S‑4, S‑11) requires prior‑period financials be retrospectively revised and reissued; new registration statement after a drop‑down — if post‑drop‑down interim financials have not been recast, prior‑periods are not revised (registrant may present supplemental historical financial statements); if interim financials have been recast and filed, prior‑period financials must be retrospectively revised. Prior‑period financials do not have to be revised unless there has been a 'fundamental change' (a legal question — consult counsel). Item 302 of Reg S‑K requires summarized quarterly information when a material retrospective change impacts recent quarters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drop‑down transactions and failed sale‑leaseback accounting — Form 8‑K reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Drop‑down transactions to an MLP that are accounted for as failed sale‑leaseback transactions under Topic 842 may be accounted for as financings under US GAAP, but the SEC staff continues to view such drop‑downs as acquisitions from the MLP perspective.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As a result, the transaction remains subject to the reporting requirements under Item 2.01 of Form 8‑K and the Item 9.01 financial statement requirements when the acquisition is that of a business under the SEC’s definition. Registrants may contact the SEC staff for interpretations or relief from providing financial information under S‑X Rule 3‑13 when facts warrant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tests of significance — scope and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Significance tests determine whether an acquisition is significant for SEC filing purposes and must be performed in specific contexts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contexts include consummated business acquisitions (Form 8‑K), when filing a registration or proxy statement, aggregate testing of individually insignificant acquisitions, and when reissuing financial statements. The guidance lists specific questions and examples for each context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Financial statement periods and data used for significance tests
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on which financial statement periods and types of financial information may be used to perform the significance tests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Questions addressed include: what financial statement period is used, whether interim periods may be used, whether financial information for a period not yet required to be filed can be used, whether unaudited financial statements of the acquired business can be used, and what to do when no previous stand‑alone financial statements exist.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consistency of fiscal year‑ends and period selection
rubrics_metrics.description: Considerations about whether registrant and acquired business fiscal year‑ends need to be consistent and whether periods used to determine aggregate significance can change from those used at acquisition date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes examples (acquisition shortly after year‑end) and procedures for identifying the fiscal year to use when calculating significance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accounting standards consistency and use of private company alternatives
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether amounts used in significance tests need to be determined under the same accounting standards and whether unadjusted amounts (including private company accounting alternatives) can be used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Questions include whether a registrant can use unadjusted amounts of the acquired business and whether adjustments are permitted to the acquired business financial statements for the tests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of pro forma information in significance tests
rubrics_metrics.description: When pro forma information may be used to perform significance tests and limitations on such use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Topics: when pro forma can be used (including prior significant acquisitions), whether pro forma includes financing effects, use of pro forma filed voluntarily on Form 8‑K for subsequent acquisitions, handling when pro forma lacks a balance sheet as of latest fiscal year‑end, and special rules for shell companies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rounding and inclusion/exclusion rules in significance calculations
rubrics_metrics.description: Mechanical and judgmental rules for performing significance calculations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Questions: Is a registrant permitted to round the results of significance tests? Does a registrant include the acquired business’s assets, income or revenues in the denominator? Are intercompany transactions between the registrant and the acquired business excluded? How are intercompany eliminations handled in the tests?

rubrics_metrics.name: Aggregation of individually insignificant acquisitions — period and method
rubrics_metrics.description: How individually insignificant acquisitions are aggregated and over what period for testing aggregate significance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers identifying individually insignificant acquisitions to aggregate, the period of time over which to aggregate, and examples on aggregation and testing (e.g., series of acquisitions, acquisitions in interim periods).

rubrics_metrics.name: Investment test — numerator and denominator (AWMV)
rubrics_metrics.description: The investment test compares the investment in and advances to the acquired business (numerator) to the registrant’s aggregate worldwide market value (denominator, AWMV) or other prescribed bases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides detailed Q&A on how investments and advances are determined, whether contingent consideration and transaction costs are included in purchase price, treatment for equity‑method investments and asset acquisitions, how to determine purchase price for staged acquisitions, how to determine AWMV, and when the AWMV must be re‑calculated after announcement date delays or changes. Also addresses exceptions to using AWMV and how to determine the denominator in aggregate tests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of contingent consideration and transaction costs in purchase price
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether contingent consideration, transaction costs, and other payments negotiated in contemplation of the acquisition are included in the purchase price for the investment test.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Multiple questions: are contingent consideration and transaction costs included when the acquisition is a business combination, when acquiring an equity‑method investment, or when the transaction is an asset acquisition; are other negotiated payments included; are transaction costs included when acquiring an equity‑method investment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purchase price determination for business acquisitions achieved in stages
rubrics_metrics.description: How to determine the purchase price for an acquisition achieved in stages (step acquisition) when applying the investment test.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes example scenarios for step acquisitions completed within a 12‑month period or without obtaining control, and guidance for investments where control is obtained in stages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determining AWMV and special considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: How the registrant’s aggregate worldwide market value (AWMV) is determined and special considerations in its calculation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Questions address how AWMV is determined, whether it should be re‑calculated after significant delays or changes between announcement and agreement dates, how to determine denominator in aggregate investment tests, what to do when registrant does not have an AWMV, and exceptions to using AWMV.

rubrics_metrics.name: Income test — pretax income and revenue components
rubrics_metrics.description: The income test has two components — pretax income and revenue — each with its own measurement rules and interaction in determining significance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance covers how the two components interact, how pretax income component is determined (including registrant’s share when there is noncontrolling interest), treatment of pretax losses, when an average of multiple years is used, combining pretax losses and income in aggregate testing, and specific issues when acquiring equity‑method investments with fair value option. Also covers revenue component determination, when revenue is 'material', registrant’s share of revenue with NCI, and aggregate income testing when not all acquired businesses have material revenue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special tests and examples (assets test, predecessor/successor statements, interim periods)
rubrics_metrics.description: Various special situations addressed in examples and additional Q&A related to significance testing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include asset test when a private company becomes a PBE through acquisition, significance calculation following common control combinations, excluding intercompany preferred stock dividends from tests, excluding intercompany receivables and profit, using periods less than 12 months, predecessor and successor financial statements, and performing tests when interim periods or pro forma balance sheets are not filed.
